content.title: 76ers vs. Hornets: Prediction, How to Watch for Free (3/28/26)
content.text: The Philadelphia 76ers (40–33) face the Charlotte Hornets (39–34) tonight at Spectrum Center in Charlotte in a potential play-in tournament preview. Charlotte comes in red-hot, having won five straight games, including a 114–103 victory over the New York Knicks on Thursday. Kon Knueppel continues his stellar rookie campaign, scoring 26 points with the bulk of that coming on six 3-pointers. Knueppel grabbed 11 boards and missed a triple-double by two assists. LaMelo Ball added 22 points, Brandon Miller scored 21, and Miles Bridges and Coby White finished with 17 apiece, showcasing Charlotte’s offensive balance. The Hornets sit in eighth place in the Eastern Conference, a game behind the seventh-place Sixers. Both teams are currently positioned for the top two play-in tournament spots, but remain in contention for an automatic playoff berth. Philadelphia, meanwhile, comes in off a dominant 157–137 win over the Chicago Bulls, with Joel Embiid’s return catalyzing one of their most explosive offensive performances of the season. Embiid scored 35 on 12-of-17 shooting. Paul George added 28 in his return from suspension, and rookie VJ Edgecombe, who had helped carry the team with their veteran stars out this month, scored 22 on an efficient 7-of-9 night from the floor. The Sixers shot a blistering 55% from the field overall and 47% from deep, capitalizing on the Bulls’ porous defense. Tyrese Maxey remains out for the Sixers, but with Embiid, George, and Edgecombe on the floor, they have the firepower to contend against most lineups. Still, the Hornets have the edge here with their abundance of scorers and efficiency from deep. Prediction: Charlotte Hornets 118, Philadelphia 76ers 113 Injury Report Philadelphia 76ers Tyrese Maxey — Out (Finger) Kelly Oubre Jr. — Out (Elbow) Johni Broome — Out (Knee) Charlotte Hornets Tidjane Salaün — Out (Calf) How to Watch 76ers vs. Hornets Tip-off for tonight’s 76ers-Hornets game is set for 6:00 PM Eastern at Spectrum Center in Charlotte. The game airs live locally on FanDuel Sports Network Southeast and NBC Sports Philadelphia. Out-of-market viewers can stream the matchup on NBA League Pass for free on Amazon Prime Video with a 7-day free trial here. Amazon also offers a discounted subscription that starts at $12.74 for the first two months (then $16.99/month). The subscription also includes access to NBA TV. Fans can also choose a Team Pass to follow one team’s games for $13.99 per month.
